findings.element: card stack (white / blue / amber cards) against the timeline and the Dec dot
findings.problem: The stack collides with the timeline. The amber back card (bottom ≈ y448 canvas) runs 15 px below the timeline rule at y≈433, so the rule cuts across it. The blue card's bottom-left corner (x840, y424) sits on the Dec dot. The front card's left edge is at x≈817, 15 px off the Dec column at x=832. It looks like an accident, not an overlap made on purpose.
findings.fix: Rebuild the stack on the Dec column. Front card: x=832, y=208, w=336, h=176. Blue card offset +24/+24 (x856, y232), amber card +48/+48 (x880, y256), so the amber right edge lands on the 1216 margin and its bottom is at y=432. Move the timeline rule and dots down to y=480 (48 px clear of the stack) and the month labels to top y=504. Keep the rule from x=64 to x=1216. Nothing may touch or cross the stack.

findings.element: slide 2 statement and slide 4 headline and stat row
findings.problem: Slides 2 and 4 make the same claim twice in a six-slide deck: slide 2 says 'uptime held above 99% … across all 41 sites', and slide 4's headline says '99.3% uptime across 41 sites', then repeats 99.3% and 41 as stats. Slide 4's three stats also have no dominant element. All three are 96 px blue, and the visual gaps are uneven: about 90 px from '99.3%' to '41', then about 290 px of hole from '41' to '6 h'.
findings.fix: Merge them: delete slide 2 and make slide 4 the uptime slide. New headline at 44 px on one line: 'Sensor uptime held at 99.3% all quarter'. Set '99.3%' alone as the hero stat at 160 px / 800, blue, at x=64 (top y=232), with the label 'uptime, July–September' at 22 px 24 px below it. Move '41 · sites live' and '6 h · median repair time' into a right column at x=832, number 56 px ink 700 and label 22 px, with 48 px between the two pairs. Use a non-breaking space in '6 h'. If slide 2 is kept instead, break its headline as 'Sensor uptime held / above 99% all quarter' and rewrite slide 4 around the 6 h repair time; the merge is preferred.

findings.element: bar chart frame and source line
findings.problem: The chart fills only x≈79–817 (canvas). Its axis starts 15 px inside the 64 margin, and the right third of the slide is empty apart from a source line floating at x≈880, y≈573. That line aligns with nothing and reads as left-over space, not a framed chart.
findings.fix: Set the chart frame to x=64, w=1152, y=232, h=344, with the axis rule starting exactly at x=64 and bars 176 px wide on equal gaps. Move the source to a 14 px footnote right-aligned to x=1216 on the same baseline as the 'Northstar Demo' footer (y≈653). Keep the 120k/190k/290k direct labels and the single full-blue Sep bar.

findings.element: region table (x 64–704) and the empty right half
findings.problem: The table takes the left 640 px. The right 512 px is dead space, and the slide makes the viewer do arithmetic to see that 17 of 41 is the largest share. The headline's claim is not visible at a glance.
findings.fix: Widen the table to x=64–1216 and add a bar column. Region text column x=64–304. Bar column x=320–1024: bar length = sites ÷ 17 × 704 px, height 24, North in blue #2E4BD8, Central and South in the 30% blue tint used on slide 3, no bar on Total. Sites stay right-aligned at x=1216. Keep the row heights and the North row tint.

findings.element: accent roles across slides 1–6 (amber, blue, the blue footer wordmark)
findings.problem: The brand reserves amber for the one highlight per slide, but amber appears only as decoration (the slide-1 bar and the back card on slide 6). Blue does every job: the footer wordmark on 5 slides, the highlighted bar, all the stats, the timeline dots and the table tint. So no colour means 'this is the one thing', and the deck has no recurring device until the last slide.
findings.fix: Make the slide-1 amber rule (48×6 px, #F2A541) the highlight marker on every content slide, placed 16 px above the one key figure. Slide 3: centred above the '290k' label. Slide 4: above '99.3%' at x=64. Slide 5: as a 6×64 px vertical bar at x=64 on the North row. Slide 6: the amber back card is already the marker. Never use amber for text, because it fails contrast on white. Set the footer 'Northstar Demo' in muted ink (#14213D at 60%, ≈#727A8B), weight 700, so blue means data only.

findings.element: headline 'Next: 20 more sites by Q1' and card '20 sites / planned by Q1'
findings.problem: The card repeats the headline word for word, so the slide's evidence adds nothing. The headline is also set at 56 px while slides 3–5 use 44 px at the same top position, so it visibly jumps when advancing from 5 to 6. It breaks with a runt ('by Q1').
findings.fix: Headline at 44 px on one line (box w=720): '20 more sites go live by Q1'. Card: '61 sites' at 56 px / 800 blue, then 'in the network by Q1 (41 today)' at 22 px ink, 16 px below. Inside the 336×176 card use 32 px padding on all sides, so the text block is centred vertically rather than top-heavy (current padding is about 43 px top and 67 px bottom).

findings.element: subtitle 'A synthetic deck for a review-regression pilot. Every number in it is fictional.'
findings.problem: The subtitle describes the tooling, not the quarter. To a leadership audience 'review-regression pilot' is noise, and it is the second thing they read.
findings.fix: Subtitle (28 px lead, same position): 'Field network · July–September'. Move the disclaimer to a 14 px footnote at x=64, baseline y=653 (the footer line used on the other slides): 'All figures are synthetic.'

findings.element: headline 'Monthly readings grew 2.4× from July to September'
findings.problem: The headline wraps with 'September' alone on line 2, a one-word runt at 44 px. The two-line headline also pushes the chart down compared with slide 5's one-line headline.
findings.fix: Rewrite it to fit on one line: 'Monthly readings grew 2.4× in Q3' (the axis already names Jul–Sep). Keep the headline top position and leave 48 px from its baseline to the chart top.

findings.problem: The 88 px and 96 px sizes sit too close to read as two levels. Inter is used in four weights (400, 600, 700, 800).
findings.fix: Use one 96 px step for the slide-1 hero (the new 160 px uptime stat on slide 4 is the only larger size). Drop weight 600: table headers and the footer go to 700, leaving 400 / 700 / 800.

findings.element: table cell text inset and Total row rule
findings.problem: Cell text starts at x=80, a second left edge 16 px inside the headline's x=64. The Total row is separated by the same 1 px grey hairline as the data rows, so it doesn't read as a sum.
findings.fix: Set cell padding-left to 0 so Region text sits at x=64, and extend the North row tint out to x=48 so the fill still clears the text. Draw a 2 px ink (#14213D) rule above the Total row instead of the hairline.

findings.element: right half of the title slide (x 760–1216 empty)
findings.problem: The brand's only motif, the card stack, appears just once at the end, so it reads as a one-off rather than a brand device. The title slide's right half is empty.
findings.fix: Bookend the deck: put the same three-card stack on slide 1 at x=832, y=232, front card 336×176 with the ink ground showing through (white 2 px outline, blue and amber cards at +24/+48 offsets). Leave the card empty, or set 'Q3' in it at 56 px white. Keep it at exactly the slide-6 geometry so the two slides rhyme.

keep: Slide 1: the 96 px title box sits 4 px left of the 64 margin, which optically aligns the 'Q' with the brand name and subtitle. This is correct optical alignment, not a near-miss.
A consistent 64 px left margin and the same headline top on slides 3–6
Slide 3: only the Sep bar is in full blue, Jul/Aug in a clean blue tint, values labelled directly, no gridlines, and a real × in '2.4×'
Slide 5: right-aligned numerals, the single tinted North row, and a heavy ink rule under the header
Slides 4 and 6 share the x=64/448/832 column grid. Keep it when re-laying out both slides.
Inter only, no off-palette colours, and real middle dots in 'Oct · 6 sites'
dismissed_lint: Slide 1 near-miss ×3 and margin 60 vs 64: the hero title box is offset 4 px (≈4% of 96 px) as an optical side-bearing correction; on the render the glyph edge lines up with the 64 px margin. Deliberate, so no change.
summary: Clean, on-brand and correctly typed, but not shippable. The closing card stack collides with its timeline. Slides 2 and 4 repeat the same uptime claim. Slides 3 and 5 leave a third to half of the slide empty, and amber never does its brand job of marking the one thing. Four headlines break with runts.
